overview: The Grizzly Bear Mine was located in 1875 in the Bear Creek section of the Ouray Mining District and developed principally as a gold-silver property.
New Mexico Bureau of Geology research reports almost $1 million in period ore value from 1875 through 1910.

timeline.text: The Grizzly Bear Mine was located in 1875 in the Bear Creek section of the Ouray Mining District and developed principally as a gold-silver property.
New Mexico Bureau of Geology research reports almost $1 million in period ore value from 1875 through 1910.

A major 1896–1900 development campaign improved the mine road, added a boarding house, and extended several tunnels by hundreds of feet, illustrating the transportation and infrastructure challenges of this steep canyon setting.

moreHistory: A major 1896–1900 development campaign improved the mine road, added a boarding house, and extended several tunnels by hundreds of feet, illustrating the transportation and infrastructure challenges of this steep canyon setting.
Surviving identification features include scattered mine machinery, collapsed structural remains, dumps, and the disturbed mine landscape; do not reconstruct intact buildings from these remnants.
Keep the historic mine workings, the related Bear Creek transportation corridor, and any later haulage-tunnel development as separate linked components.
The reported dollar figure is a historical period value, not a modern valuation.
No unsupported lifetime tonnage is stated.
